I've been farming this 3 mu plot for years. Stevia is my livelihood — the processing companies in the area buy my dried leaf, and they test for stevioside content, so I can't just chase bulk yield. I need quality.

I'll plant all 3 mu in stevia again this spring, like always. I'll transplant seedlings from improved varieties in late April once the ground is warm and the last frost risk is gone here in southern Hebei. I use rotary tillage before transplanting — stevia roots need loose, well-drained soil or they rot, especially when I irrigate.

On fertilizer, I'm careful with nitrogen. I've learned the hard way that heavy nitrogen pushes leafy growth but drops the sweetness. The buyers dock me on price if stevioside content is low. I'll apply around 10 kg N per mu — base fertilizer before planting plus a top-dress after first cutting. Phosphorus around 5 kg, potassium around 8 kg to keep the plants strong through the hot summer.

With the well, I can irrigate reliably. I usually irrigate about 10 times through the season — at establishment, then when the plants are setting leaf mass, and through any dry stretches in July and August.

I'll spray pesticide 3 times — once preventive for aphids early on, once mid-season for powdery mildew which we get when it's humid, and once more if I see pressure. I don't spray more than I have to; it costs money and the buyers sometimes ask about residues.

I expect around 250 kg of dried leaf per mu if the summer isn't too harsh. Some years I get two cuttings, some years one good one. I plan for one solid harvest.
